name: Xiakucao (Prunella vulgaris, self-heal)
short: In a 12-week placebo-controlled trial in 80 men, adverse events were low and similar to placebo. In thyroid trials it was added to thyroid drugs, with adverse reactions not more frequent.
text: In a 12-week randomised, placebo-controlled trial of Prunella vulgaris extract in 80 men aged 40 to 75 with urinary symptoms, the incidence of adverse events was low and similar between groups. Most other evidence comes from trials in which Prunella preparations were added to thyroid medicines: a meta-analysis of 13 trials (1468 patients) with thyroid nodules found an adverse reaction risk ratio of 0.67 (95% CI 0.36 to 1.22) compared with the medicine alone, a difference that was not statistically significant, and a meta-analysis of 17 trials (1,366 patients) with hyperthyroidism reported fewer adverse events when Prunella preparations were combined with antithyroid drugs than with antithyroid drugs alone. The authors of both reviews rated the quality of the evidence as uncertain or low. The abstracts do not describe specific adverse effects. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
